title: Material Acquisition
scope: GKI-05: where and how each of the 108 ship engineering materials can be obtained: the material records not already held by other packs, the acquisition activities with their procedures, conditions and equipment, and community-reported Crystalline Shard, Brain Tree and wreckage sites.
game_version: Reflects the cited wiki revisions as read on 2026-10-30 (current game) and community reports from 2025. Fungal growths on Brain Trees and other fungal life are a documented raw material source; ship-based limpet harvesting at surface sites was reported broken in March 2025, so the SRV method is the one offered.
rights_basis: Original OmniCOVAS records of Elite Dangerous game facts: material names, grades, sources, conditions, equipment and procedures, written in OmniCOVAS's own words. No wiki prose, tables or images are reproduced; sources are credited per claim and per relationship.

distribution.basis: GKI-05 content audit (2026-10-30, corrected at the final review the same day): every record is an original statement of game facts, checked with the curator expression check against the cited wiki revisions; community guides and forum reports are restated as facts only.

entities.name: Cargo scoop
entities.summary: Ship module that collects floating materials and canisters.

claims.text: Free-floating materials in signal sources and ship wreckage are taken aboard with a cargo scoop.

entities.name: Frame Shift Wake Scanner
entities.summary: Utility module that scans high energy wakes.

claims.text: High energy wakes can only be scanned with this utility module, which must be in a fire group.

entities.name: Detailed Surface Scanner
entities.summary: Ship module for mapping bodies with probes.

claims.text: Mapping a body reveals its geological signals and which raw materials its surface can yield.

entities.name: Recon limpet controller
entities.summary: Limpet controller used to hack installation and megaship systems.

claims.text: Comms arrays and data transmitters are hacked with recon limpets after a data link scan.

entities.name: Mining tools
entities.summary: Mining laser or other ship mining equipment.

claims.text: Raw materials turn up as fragments while mining asteroids with ship mining tools.

entities.name: High Grade Emissions
entities.summary: Deep-space signal sources holding very rare manufactured materials, set by the system's allegiance and its factions' states.

hge_rules.label: faction in War or Civil War
faction in Outbreak in a system of over a million people

steps.text: Look for High Grade Emissions in the system's signal list; they are commonest in systems of a million people or more.
If none show, scanning the nav beacon can make one appear.
Drop in, check the contacts panel for the material you want, then collect it with the cargo scoop.

claims.text: Each signal belongs to one minor faction. Federation and Empire allegiance gives composites or shielding; elsewhere the faction's state decides: War or Civil War, Civil Unrest, Boom or Expansion, or Outbreak in a populous system.

Sources differ on whose allegiance counts: the wiki speaks of both the controlling faction and the signal's own faction, and a community guide names the system's allegiance. OmniCOVAS goes by the system's allegiance and marks other cases as uncertain.
In Federation and Empire systems, signals are reported with no state or with Civil Liberty, which carries no state-based material.
When a faction meets more than one condition, the game picks by a hidden order, so the result for such factions is not certain.

entities.name: Degraded and other common signal sources
entities.summary: The commonest signal sources in populated space, with debris holding lower-grade manufactured materials.

steps.text: Drop into Degraded Emissions or similar signal sources in populated systems.
Collect the floating materials with the cargo scoop; some sites attract pirates.

claims.text: Unthreatened sites hold grade 1 to 3 manufactured materials among the debris; a material page may name the system state or security that favours it.

entities.name: Encoded Emissions
entities.summary: Common signal sources that may hold a data beacon, a debris field or, near inhabited Earth-like worlds, a satellite.

steps.text: Drop into Encoded Emissions in any populated system.
Scan any data beacon or satellite, and scoop the debris materials.

claims.text: Contents are random: a data beacon with lower-grade materials, a debris field with grade 2 to 4 materials, or a satellite.

entities.name: Data beacon scanning
entities.summary: Scan the black-box data beacons found among debris in emissions signal sources.

steps.text: Find a data beacon in Degraded or Encoded Emissions.
Target it, close within about 200 m and keep it centred until the scan completes.

claims.text: Beacons give mostly grade 1 and 2 encoded materials.

entities.name: Satellite scanning
entities.summary: Scan communication satellites near inhabited Earth-like worlds and some installations for encoded materials.

steps.text: Orbit an inhabited Earth-like world in supercruise until Encoded Emissions appear, then drop in.
Target the satellite and keep it centred to scan.

claims.text: Satellites yield encoded materials such as firmware and encryption data.

entities.name: Scanning ships
entities.summary: Target a ship and keep it centred: the ship's sensors may yield shield, emission or scan data.

steps.text: Target a ship in supercruise or normal space and hold it in the centre of view until the scan completes.

claims.text: A scan only sometimes yields data, and which data depends on the kind of ship.

entities.name: High energy wake scanning
entities.summary: Scan the high energy wakes ships leave when jumping to another system.

steps.text: Fit a Frame Shift Wake Scanner and put it in a fire group.
Target a high energy wake in the contacts panel, stay close and hold fire until the scan completes.
Busy systems produce more wakes to scan.

claims.text: The scanner page lists wake data of grades 1 to 4; the grade 5 material's own page also names wakes at busy sites, which the scanner page does not.

entities.name: Settlement data points
entities.summary: Scan data points at surface installations and settlements from the SRV; higher security gives rarer data.

steps.text: Land near a surface installation or settlement and deploy the SRV.
Scan each data point with the SRV's Data Link Scanner; sets of points must all be scanned.
Higher security sites give rarer data but defend themselves more strongly.

claims.text: Outposts come in low, medium and high security; the rarer data is at the better defended ones.
Surface scan missions point to small settlements whose data points often give rare and very rare data.

entities.name: Hacking installation and megaship systems
entities.summary: Data-link scan an installation or megaship, then hack its comms array or data transmitter with recon limpets.

steps.text: Use the Data Link Scanner on the installation or megaship first, and next on its comms array or transmitter.
Hack it with a recon limpet.
Outside Anarchy systems this calls security and gives a bounty; silent running reduces but does not remove the risk.

claims.text: Hacking is a crime outside Anarchy systems.

entities.name: Military and authority ship salvage
entities.summary: Materials dropped by destroyed military and system authority ships, found in conflict zones and policed systems.

steps.text: Destroying system authority ships makes you wanted; conflict zones offer lawful military targets.
Collect the dropped materials with the cargo scoop.

claims.text: Military and authority ships patrol populated non-Anarchy systems; War and Civil Unrest add conflict zones.

entities.name: Ship salvage (any ship)
entities.summary: Materials dropped by destroyed ships of any role; bigger ships tend to drop higher grades.

steps.text: Destroy a ship lawfully, for example a wanted ship, and scoop what it drops.

claims.text: Larger ships usually drop the higher grades.

entities.name: Crystalline Shard sites
entities.summary: Geological sites on cold, airless volcanic bodies far from their star, where crystalline clusters hold high-grade raw materials.

steps.text: Travel to a reported site; the nearest known ones are about 1,500 light years from Sol.
Map the body with probes to find its geological signals.
Land, deploy the SRV, break the crystalline clusters and scoop the materials.

claims.text: Shards grow on airless volcanic bodies at least 12,000 light seconds from the nearest star.
Site lists are compiled from commander reports; which raw material a site gives depends on the body.

entities.name: Volcanic geological sites
entities.summary: Needle crystals at lava spouts and crystalline fragments at other geological signals hold rare raw materials.

steps.text: Map a body with volcanism to find geological signals.
Land at the signal, find the crystals with the SRV wave scanner, break them and scoop the materials.

claims.text: Needle crystals occur at some lava spout sites on volcanic terrestrial bodies.

entities.name: Fungal growths (Brain Trees and other fungal life)
entities.summary: Growths on Brain Trees and other fungal life on airless bodies drop raw materials when shot; which ones depends on the planet.

steps.text: Go to a reported Brain Tree or fungal site; fungal life grows on airless bodies, and Brain Trees mostly on volcanic ones.
Land, deploy the SRV and find the growths with its wave scanner.
Shoot the growths and scoop the raw materials they drop with the SRV.

claims.text: Four growth types drop different grades: Cordycep Growths very common (grade 1), Polyporous Growths common (grade 2) and some rare ones, Mussidaen Seed Pods standard (grade 3) and Phloem Excretions rare (grade 4).
Which material of that grade a growth gives depends on the planet's composition, so a reported site matters.

Community guides also describe breaking growths from the ship with remote release flak and gathering them with collector limpets. In March 2025 commanders reported their limpets being destroyed at these sites after a change to limpet behaviour, while the SRV method still worked.
In 2025 commanders also reported visits where some growth types did not appear at patches they had used before; the cause was not confirmed.

entities.name: Cargo racks at surface wreckage
entities.summary: Cargo racks among ship wreckage on planet surfaces release materials when destroyed.

steps.text: Find ship wreckage on a planet surface; a reported crash site saves searching.
Shoot the cargo racks from the ship or an SRV.
Scoop the canisters they release with the ship's or the SRV's cargo scoop.

claims.text: Each destroyed rack releases one or two different materials.
